description:
A SWML document for handling inbound SMS, MMS, WhatsApp, or RCS messages. The document has a top-level
`sections` map; execution starts at `sections.main`, and each section is an ordered array of
methods. Additional sections can be invoked via `execute`, `transfer`, or `goto`.

See the [Messaging SWML reference](/docs/swml/reference/messaging) for the full list of
available methods.
title: Messaging SWML Document

reply.description:
Create and send an outbound message in response to the inbound message. The reply goes
out on the inbound message's channel: SMS or MMS, WhatsApp, or RCS. Accepts one of: a
string (used as the message body), an object with content and routing fields, or an
inline `switch` that branches the reply on a variable value.

`reply` does not end execution — subsequent steps in the section continue to run after
the reply is queued.
reply.title: reply

receive.description: Accept the inbound message without sending a reply. No-op step.
receive.title: receive

url.description: Endpoint to call. Must be a publicly reachable URL.

headers.description: HTTP headers to include with the request, as a map of header name to value. Each value must be a string.

body.description:
Request body, always sent JSON-encoded. An object is sent as a JSON object. A
string is sent as a JSON string value, with quotes and escaping, not as raw text.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Clamped to a maximum of `5.0`.

save_variables.description:
If `true`, parse the response into `request_response.*` variables. Fields are
saved when the URL returns a 2xx response whose body is a JSON object; nothing is
saved from 4xx or 5xx responses.

request.description:
Make an HTTP request from inside your SWML document — useful for looking up
records, calling your own API, or fetching data to use later in the message flow.

After the request, the `%{request_result}` variable tells you the outcome:

- `"success"` — the URL returned a 2xx response.
- `"failed"` — the URL returned a response outside the 2xx range, such as a 4xx
  or 5xx.
- `"timeout"` — the request didn't get a response within `timeout` seconds, or
  the connection to the URL failed.
- `"limit_exceeded"` — your document already made the maximum of 10 requests;
  this call was skipped.

Timeouts, connection failures, and unsuccessful HTTP responses don't stop your
document — the next steps still run, so you can branch on `%{request_result}` to
handle each outcome. Omitting `url`, or a `url` that expands to an empty value,
is a fatal error that stops the document.

When `save_variables` is `true` and the URL returns a 2xx response whose body is
a JSON object, the parsed fields are available as `%{request_response.<field>}`.
The response status code is in `%{request_response_code}` as a string (for
example `"200"`) and the response body in `%{request_response_body}`. The stored
body is a string, truncated to its first 65,536 characters after the response
is received; responses with a JSON content type are stored as re-serialized
JSON, so formatting can differ from what the server sent.
request.title: request

dest.description:
Where to execute. One of:

- The name of a section in the current document.
- A URL (`http` or `https`) that returns a messaging SWML document.
  SignalWire fetches it with a `POST` request carrying the inbound message
  webhook payload, with `params` set to the values supplied here and `vars` set
  to the caller's current variables.
- An inline messaging SWML document, supplied as a string that holds the whole
  document serialized as a JSON object. A string that isn't a valid JSON object
  is treated as a section name.

params.description: Parameters accessible as `params.*` in the called section or document. Replaces (does not merge with) any outer `params` from the caller.

execute.description:
Run a section, a SWML document fetched from a URL, or an inline SWML document as a
subroutine. Execution continues in the called section or document, then returns to
the caller when it completes — either via `return` or by reaching the end. A called
document starts at its `sections.main`.

A called section runs with the caller's variables, with `params` replaced. A called
URL or inline document starts fresh: it sees the inbound `message` and the `params`
supplied here, but not the caller's other variables, such as `request_result`.

Accepts either a destination string (shorthand) or an object with `dest` and
`params`. The shorthand calls the destination with empty `params`, and `%{...}`
references in it are not expanded; use the object form to build the destination
or pass parameters from variables.
execute.title: execute

dest.description:
Where to transfer. One of:

- The name of a section in the current document.
- A URL (`http` or `https`) to fetch the new SWML document from. Authentication
  can be embedded in the URL as `username:password@url`.
- An inline SWML document, supplied as a string that holds the whole document
  serialized as a JSON object. A YAML or JSON object nested directly under `dest`
  is not accepted, and a string that isn't a valid JSON object is treated as a
  section name. Execution starts at its `sections.main`.

`%{...}` variable references in `dest` are expanded before the destination is
resolved.

method.description: HTTP method for the fetch request. Used only when `dest` is a URL.

params.description:
Parameters for the transferred section or document, available there as `params.*`.
When `dest` is a URL, they are also sent in the request body. They replace the
current `params` rather than merging with them; when omitted, the target receives
an empty object.

String values are expanded for `%{...}` variable references at every depth,
including inside nested objects and arrays. Keys are not expanded. Each
substitution produces a string, a reference to a path that doesn't exist becomes
an empty string, and expressions are not evaluated.

transfer.description:
Hand processing over to another section, another SWML document fetched from a URL,
or an inline SWML document. `dest` selects which.

This is a tail call: it does not return, and steps after `transfer`, including
steps in calling sections, are skipped. A URL or inline destination also replaces
the current document.

When `dest` is a URL, SignalWire sends the
[inbound message webhook payload](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/inbound-message-webhook)
in the request body to `dest`, using `method` (`POST` by default): `message`
describes the original inbound message, `params` carries the values supplied here,
and `vars` carries the propagated runtime variables (`request_result`,
`reply_result`, etc.) accumulated by the current document.
transfer.title: transfer

variable.description:
Variable path to match. Specified without the `%{}` wrapper (e.g. `message.body`).
The resolved value is converted to a string, then transformed and compared exactly
with the `case` keys. A missing variable path resolves to an empty string.

transform.description: Transform to apply to the value before matching.

case.description:
Map of values to arrays of SWML methods to execute. The key is the value to compare
against `variable` (after applying `transform`); the value is the array of methods
to run on match. Keys are literal and are not transformed, and matching is exact.
An empty-string key matches a missing variable; otherwise `default` is used.

default.description:
Array of SWML methods to execute if no `case` matches. If omitted and no case
matches, execution stops with an error.

switch.description:
Branch on a variable's value, with optional text transforms applied before matching.
Useful for keyword-driven inbound message handling.

After the selected branch runs, execution continues with the next step after
`switch`, unless the branch moves execution elsewhere (for example with `goto`,
`return`, or `transfer`), a step fails, or the document reaches its 100-step limit.
switch.title: switch

label.description: Label to jump to. Must reference a `label` step in the current section.

max.description:
Maximum number of jumps to `label`. Accepts an integer or a `%{...}` variable
reference; a reference is expanded and then converted to an integer. A reference
that doesn't resolve allows no jumps — it does not fall back to 100.

Jumps are counted per target label for the whole run, not per `goto` step: every
`goto` that targets the same label name shares one count, including `goto` steps
in other sections and in documents reached through `execute` or `transfer`. Each
jump attempt adds one to the count and is allowed while the count is at most this
step's `max`.

When an attempt exceeds `max`, the jump doesn't happen and the steps array that
contains the label ends without running its remaining steps. Execution continues
with whatever ran that array, such as the steps after an enclosing `switch` or
the caller of an `execute`.

`max` cannot raise the document's limit of 100 steps, which counts every step
including each `label` passed. That limit can stop execution before `max` jumps
are reached. If the limit is reached on the `goto` step itself, the jump never
happens and the run ends with a `swml_goto_label_not_found` error.

goto.description:
Jump to a named label in the current section. Used for retry loops and conditional
repetition. `goto` does not cross subroutine boundaries.

Accepts a label name as a string (shorthand) or an object with `label` and `max`.
The shorthand jumps to the label exactly as written, without variable expansion,
with the default `max` of 100.
goto.title: goto

return.description:
Return from the current section. Inside a section or document called via `execute`,
control returns to the caller and the value is accessible as `return_value` in the
caller's context. A document run with `execute` starts at its own `main`, so a
`return` there also hands its value back to the caller. In the top-level `main`,
meaning the document handling the inbound message or a document reached through
`transfer`, there is no caller: `return` stops execution entirely and its value is
discarded. To return without a value, use `return: null`.
return.title: return

label.description:
Mark any point of the SWML section with a label so that `goto` can jump to it. Must be
unique within the section.

ReplyText.description:
Reply body text, used by the string shorthand and by string outcomes of an inline
`switch`. After variable expansion it must contain at least one non-whitespace
character.

Body length is checked before the reply is queued. The limit depends on the channel
(SMS, MMS, WhatsApp, or RCS) and on the route SignalWire uses to send the reply, and length is counted
according to the message encoding. A body over the limit fails the reply with a
`swml_reply_character_limit_exceeded` error whose message states the limit.
ReplyText.title: Reply body text

to.description:
Destination phone number in E.164 format. Defaults to the inbound message's `from`; on
WhatsApp, a leading `+` is added to it. On RCS it must be a US number.

from.description:
Sender of the reply. Defaults to the inbound message's `to`, so the reply comes from the
number or agent that received the message. For SMS and MMS, a phone number or short code
owned by your project with messaging capability. For WhatsApp, a WhatsApp number in your
project, prefixed with `whatsapp:`. For RCS, the ID of an RCS agent in your project.

status_url.description:
HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives delivery status callbacks for the outbound reply. The
callback uses the [message status callback payload](/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/message-status-callback).
Callbacks are delivered after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm
that a callback reached this URL.

body.description:
Body text of the reply. For SMS and MMS, required if `media` is not present. When no
media is attached, the body must contain at least one non-whitespace character after
variable expansion.

Body length is checked before the reply is queued. The limit depends on the channel
(SMS, MMS, WhatsApp, or RCS) and on the route SignalWire uses to send the reply, and length is counted
according to the message encoding. A body over the limit fails the reply with a
`swml_reply_character_limit_exceeded` error whose message states the limit.

media.description:
Array of HTTP or HTTPS media URLs to attach. Converts the message to MMS. Maximum 8
attachments. Media is fetched after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not
confirm that the media could be retrieved.

SMS and MMS only. A WhatsApp reply ignores `media`, and an RCS reply that sets it fails
with `rcs_media_not_supported`.

Destination phone number in E.164 format. Defaults to the inbound message's `from`; on
WhatsApp, a leading `+` is added to it. On RCS it must be a US number.

Sender of the reply. Defaults to the inbound message's `to`, so the reply comes from the
number or agent that received the message. For SMS and MMS, a phone number or short code
owned by your project with messaging capability. For WhatsApp, a WhatsApp number in your
project, prefixed with `whatsapp:`. For RCS, the ID of an RCS agent in your project.

HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives delivery status callbacks for the outbound reply. The

Callbacks are delivered after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm
that a callback reached this URL.

media.description:
Array of HTTP or HTTPS media URLs to attach. Converts the message to MMS. Required if
`body` is not present, and must then contain at least one URL. Maximum 8 attachments.
Media is fetched after the reply is queued, so a `queued` result does not confirm that
the media could be retrieved.

SMS and MMS only. A WhatsApp reply ignores `media`, so it needs a `body` or `template_id`
instead, and an RCS reply that sets it fails with `rcs_media_not_supported`.

body.description:
Optional body text included alongside the media attachments. Must be a non-empty string
if provided. Body length is checked before the reply is queued. The limit depends on
the route SignalWire uses to send the reply, and length is counted according to the
message encoding. A body over the limit fails the reply with a
`swml_reply_character_limit_exceeded` error whose message states the limit.

message_type.description:
The kind of WhatsApp message to send. A WhatsApp reply without `message_type` is sent as
`whatsapp_media_text`.

body.description:
Message content, in the shape that `message_type` calls for: text for
`whatsapp_media_text`, an array of contacts for `whatsapp_media_contacts`, and an object
for every other type. These are the same shapes the
[send message API](/docs/apis/rest/messages/create-message) accepts. A string is sent as
is for text and parsed as JSON for the other types. An object or array body is counted
as its JSON text for the character limit, so a large interactive body can exceed it.

ReplyWhatsAppMessage.description:
A WhatsApp media or interactive reply. Applies only when the inbound message is a WhatsApp
message. Free-form WhatsApp messages can only be sent within 24 hours of the customer's last
inbound message.
ReplyWhatsAppMessage.title: WhatsApp reply with message type

template_id.description: The template to send, by SignalWire template ID or Meta template ID. The template must be `approved`.

header_template_parameters.description: Values for the placeholders in the template header. An array for positional parameters, an object for named parameters, or a media URL string for a document/media header.

body_template_parameters.description: Values for the placeholders in the template body. An array for positional parameters or an object for named parameters.

button_template_parameters.description: Values for URL-button placeholders. Positional only (an array); named parameters are not supported for buttons.

ReplyWhatsAppTemplate.description:
A WhatsApp template reply. Applies only when the inbound message is a WhatsApp message. Use
a template to reply more than 24 hours after the customer's last inbound message. The
template must be approved and belong to the same WhatsApp Business Account as the `from`
number. Do not set `body`.
ReplyWhatsAppTemplate.title: WhatsApp reply with template

content.description:
Rich content to send: media, a location, text with suggestions, a card, or a carousel.
The same content types as the [send message API](/docs/apis/rest/messages/create-message).

ReplyRcsContent.description:
An RCS rich-content reply. Applies only when the inbound message is an RCS message. Set
`content` or `body`, never both.
ReplyRcsContent.title: RCS reply with rich content

variable.description: Variable path to match. Specified without the `%{}` wrapper (e.g. `message.body`).

transform.description: Transform to apply to the value before matching.

case.description:
Map of values to reply outcomes. Each entry's value is either a string (used as
the reply body, sent back to the original sender) or a full reply object, in any of
the object forms `reply` accepts. Use the object form when the branch needs media,
rich content, a different destination, or a per-branch `status_url`.

default.description:
Fallback used when no `case` value matches. Same string-or-reply-object shape as a
`case` value. If omitted and no case matches, the `reply` step fails and execution
stops.

ReplyInlineSwitch.description:
Branch the reply on a variable value. The matched `case` (or `default`) supplies the
reply contents in one of two forms:

- **String** — sent back to the original sender as the reply body. The simplest form,
  good for choosing between canned text responses.
- **Reply object** — any object form of `reply`, such as `{ body, media, to, from,
  status_url }`, or a WhatsApp or RCS reply object, so the matched branch can attach
  media, send rich content, override the destination, or set a per-branch status
  callback. Any `%{…}` placeholders inside the object are expanded before the reply is
  sent.

When you use an inline `switch`, do not set `body`, `media`, `to`, `from`, or
`status_url` directly on the same `reply` — put them inside each `case` value
(or `default`) instead.
ReplyInlineSwitch.title: Reply with inline switch

SwitchTransform.description: Transform applied to the variable value before matching.
SwitchTransform.title: SwitchTransform enum

MessagingVariableReference.description:
A messaging SWML variable reference, such as `%{params.max_retries}`. It is replaced with
the variable's value from the inbound message (`message.*`), the current `params`, or a
variable set by an earlier step before the method uses it.
MessagingVariableReference.title: Messaging variable reference

WhatsAppReplyMessageType.description: The kind of WhatsApp message a reply sends. Each type sets the shape of `body`.
WhatsAppReplyMessageType.title: WhatsApp message type

link.description: A public HTTP/HTTPS URL to the image.

id.description: The ID of media previously uploaded to WhatsApp. Mutually exclusive with `link`.

caption.description: Optional caption shown with the image.

WhatsAppImageBody.description: Body for an image message. Provide either `link` or `id` (not both).

link.description: A public HTTP/HTTPS URL to the video.

id.description: The ID of media previously uploaded to WhatsApp. Mutually exclusive with `link`.

caption.description: Optional caption shown with the video.

WhatsAppVideoBody.description: Body for a video message. Provide either `link` or `id` (not both).

link.description: A public HTTP/HTTPS URL to the audio file.

id.description: The ID of media previously uploaded to WhatsApp. Mutually exclusive with `link`.

WhatsAppAudioBody.description: Body for an audio message. Provide either `link` or `id` (not both). Captions are not supported.

link.description: A public HTTP/HTTPS URL to the sticker file. Meta requires `.webp` format.

id.description: The ID of media previously uploaded to WhatsApp. Mutually exclusive with `link`.

WhatsAppStickerBody.description: Body for a sticker message. Provide either `link` or `id` (not both). Captions are not supported.

link.description: A public HTTP/HTTPS URL to the document.

id.description: The ID of media previously uploaded to WhatsApp. Mutually exclusive with `link`.

caption.description: Optional caption shown with the document.

filename.description: Optional filename shown to the recipient. Maximum 240 characters.

WhatsAppDocumentBody.description: Body for a document message. Provide either `link` or `id` (not both).

WhatsAppLocationBody.description: Body for a location message. All fields are required.

message_id.description: The ID of the message being reacted to.

WhatsAppContact.description: A shared contact card. Additional fields (phones, emails, org, etc.) follow the WhatsApp contacts message format.

action.description: The interactive action. Its contents depend on `type` (for example, a `buttons` array, list `sections`, or Flow parameters).

body.description: Optional body object, e.g. `{ "text": "How can we help?" }`.

WhatsAppInteractiveBody.description: Body for an interactive message. `type` and `action` are required; `header`, `body`, and `footer` are optional. The shape of `action` depends on the interactive type — buttons, list sections, a call-to-action URL, a location request, or a Flow — and follows the WhatsApp interactive message format.

RcsContent.description: Rich content for an RCS message. The `type` field determines the other fields.

formatted_name.description: The contact's full formatted name. Required.

WhatsAppContactName.description: The name fields of a shared contact.

url.description: An HTTP or HTTPS URL to the file.

label.description: Optional label for the pin on the map.

examples: Can you make your appointment tomorrow at 2pm?

actions.description: Suggestions shown under the text. At least one.

RcsSuggestionsContent.description: Sends text with suggestions the recipient can tap.

media.description: An HTTP or HTTPS URL to a media file shown on the card.

cards.description: The cards in the carousel. At least 1 and at most 10 cards.

actions.description: Suggestions shown under the carousel. Maximum 3.

RcsCarouselContent.description: Sends a horizontally scrolling set of rich cards.

RcsAction.description: A suggestion shown with a message. The `type` field determines the other fields.

media.description: An HTTP or HTTPS URL to a media file shown on the card.

RcsCard.description: A rich card: a title with optional subtitle, image, and suggestions.

RcsReplyAction.description: A suggested reply. Tapping it sends a reply to your agent as an inbound message.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to open.

webview.description: How the URL opens: in the device's browser, or in a webview inside the messaging app at full, half, or tall height.

RcsUrlAction.description: Opens a URL on the recipient's device.

RcsCallAction.description: Starts a phone call from the recipient's device.

label.description: Optional label for the pin on the map.

RcsLocationAction.description: Shows a location on a map on the recipient's device.

description.description: Optional description of the calendar event.

fallback_url.description: An HTTP or HTTPS URL to open when the device can't create the calendar event.

RcsCalendarAction.description: Adds an event to the recipient's calendar.

fallback_url.description: An HTTP or HTTPS URL to open when the device can't share its location.
